 Ben Duckett of England celebrates making a century against Australia during the third men’s one-day International at Hobart’s Bellerive Oval. Follow live scores for the Aus v Eng game. Follow live scores for the Aus v Eng game. Photograph: James Ross/AAP Martin Pegan (now) and Rob Smyth (later) Wed 18 Nov 2026 01.08 EST First published on Tue 17 Nov 2026 21.06 EST Share Key events 20m ago CENTURY! for Ben Duckett 
 25m ago WICKET! Archer c Edwards b Head 7 (England 195-5) 
 35m ago WICKET! Cox st Inglis b Renshaw 12 (England 172-4) 
 1h ago WICKET! Brook c Beardman b Connolly 17 (England 146-3) 
 2h ago WICKET! Root b Renshaw 12 (England 112-2) 
 2h ago WICKET! Banton c Marsh b Edwards 44 (England 74-1) 
 3h ago England XI 
 3h ago Australia XI 
 3h ago England win the toss and elect to bat 
 4h ago Preamble 
 33s ago 01.08 EST Ivor might have found a cold corner at Bellerive Oval but Vinny in Dorset has nothing but nice things to say about Hobart.
 “You’ll struggle to find a nicer spot to spend a day watching cricket than the Bellerive Oval,” Vinny says. “Fond memories of watching Australia v Sri Lanka Test match in 2012 there. Australia’s first post Ponting Test I believe. The ‘water taxi’ across the Derwent to the Oval was a highlight too.”
 Share 3m ago 01.06 EST 37th over: England 236-5 (Duckett 122, Jacks 15) SIX! Duckett slogs Head but a top edge makes it initially seem unlikely to clear Bartlett on the rope. The opener picks up three more through cover and Jacks smacks a boundary in front of point. 17 runs from the over.
 Share 8m ago 01.01 EST Ivor is trying to take his mind off the weather as he throws up a curly one for us to ponder. “Sitting freezing to death in one of the less sunny spots at Bellerive,” he says. “Not sure if it’s been mentioned but five England players have played for the Hobart Hurricanes and no Australians. If you want to push it further, can you name them?”
 I’ll leave the floor open for now and see if anyone can get all five.
 Share 9m ago 00.59 EST 36th over: England 219-5 (Duckett 112, Jacks 8) Beardman is back in the attack. Four singles come from the opening four deliveries before Duckett cashes in on being given too much room and hammers a cut to the rope. Bartlett has been back on the field for a handful of overs after getting some attention on a leg issue. He should be able to bowl again shortly after spending time away from the action.
 Share 11m ago 00.57 EST 35th over: England 210-5 (Duckett 105, Jacks 6) Duckett returns from the beverage break showing more intent now that he has already reached his milestone. The opener slog sweeps Head from well outside off stump and over deep midwicket for four. An aggressive drive takes a thick edge and falls narrowly short of a diving Beardman in the gully to short third region.
 Share 17m ago 00.52 EST A reminder that Cricket Australia has announced the creation of an independent “forum” for players and staff to share their accounts of the infamous South Africa tour of 2018 in the hope it provides a “circuit breaker” to the ongoing sandpaper saga.
 Speaking next to a children’s playground outside Bellerive Oval in Hobart before the third one-day international between Australia and England, David Boon, the interim CA chair, and chief executive Todd Greenberg insisted the intention is not to “re-litigate” events eight years ago and it will not lead to further sanctions.
 Ali Martin was in Hobart to hear all about it …
 ‘Time for a circuit breaker’: Cricket Australia creates forum for players to air views on sandpapergate Read more Share 18m ago 00.50 EST 34th over: England 204-5 (Duckett 100, Jacks 5) Duckett reaches a hundred with a clip off the pads for one. That might mark time for him to open up again but Connolly has both the England batters on a tight leash. That’s drinks.
 Share 20m ago 00.48 EST CENTURY! for Ben Duckett
 The England opener brings up his seventh ODI century and his first in Australia (this is his first series in the country) from 94 deliveries with 13 boundaries and a six. That’s his third in his past five ODIs after arriving in Australia in top form.
 Share 21m ago 00.48 EST 33rd over: England 202-5 (Duckett 99, Jacks 4) Duckett edges closer to his ton with a pair of singles as Australia have the field back saving boundaries. Head loses his grip and a loopy delivery bounces off the pitch. Jacks opens up from the freehit but the ball flies skyward and barely 10 metres from the pitch as England scamper for two.
 Share 25m ago 00.43 EST WICKET! Archer c Edwards b Head 7 (England 195-5)
 Jofra Archer slog sweeps again but this time picks out Travis Head at deep mid-wicket. The Australian fielder races in off the rope and takes a smart catch diving forward.
 Share 26m ago 00.42 EST 32nd over: England 195-4 (Duckett 97, Archer 7) Duckett starts the over hammering Connolly through the covers for four. Archer adds a second boundary with a slog sweep from down on one knee. That’s more likely what he was sent in early to do with Australia’s spinners changing the game.
 Share 30m ago 00.39 EST 31st over: England 185-4 (Duckett 92, Archer 2) SIX! Duckett opens up to move within sight of a century. The opener smacks Renshaw back over his head for the first six of the innings. Renshaw ends the over asking the question as Archer tries to switch hit him but is rapped on the pads. Looks to be sliding down leg.
 Share 33m ago 00.36 EST 30th over: England 176-4 (Duckett 84, Archer 1) Connolly continues around the wicket to Duckett and as the opener playing off the back foot with little threat. Duckett finds a single to deep midwicket and Archer gets off the mark with an inside edge.
 Share 35m ago 00.34 EST WICKET! Cox st Inglis b Renshaw 12 (England 172-4)
 Jordan Cox dances down the track but fails to get bat on ball as he is beaten in the flight and Inglis whips off the bails. Renshaw has 2 for 24 from seven overs during a gamechanging spell. Jofra Archer comes in ahead of Will Jacks.
 29th over: England 172-4 (Duckett 82, Archer 0) 
 Share Updated at  00.34 EST 38m ago 00.30 EST 28th over: England 168-3 (Duckett 80, Cox 10) Duckett finally breaks the shackles as he reverse sweeps Connolly to the boundary. But the England opener can’t find a way through the infield again.
 Share 42m ago 00.26 EST 27th over: England 163-3 (Duckett 76, Cox 9) Renshaw keeps the squeeze on England with an over filled with variation of pace and length. Cox finds a pair of singles to mid-on, with Duckett’s one off the pads in between.
 Share 45m ago 00.24 EST 26th over: England 160-3 (Duckett 75, Cox 7) Travis Head keeps spin in the attack with England tied down through the middle overs. Cox picks up a couple of singles and Duckett adds one with a late cut.
 Share 47m ago 00.22 EST Rowan Sweeney writes in to lay the boot into the England captain. “I don’t want to hear that Harry Brook failed just now,” he says. “After today’s innings he’s more than doubled his ODI average in Australia. It’s now nearly eight!”
 Share 49m ago 00.20 EST 25th over: England 157-3 (Duckett 74, Cox 5) Connolly said this week he sees himself as a batter who bowls. The 23-year-old only bowled three overs in this series before sending down his third today. Five singles and a sweep for two to Duckett keep the scoreboard ticking over.
 Share 52m ago 00.17 EST 24th over: England 150-3 (Duckett 70, Cox 2) Johnson tidies up his figures just a touch after going for 40 runs from his first four overs. He now has 0 for 45 from six. England bookend this over with a pair of singles to bring up the 150 just short of the halfway mark.
 Share 55m ago 00.13 EST 23rd over: England 148-3 (Duckett 69, Cox 1) Connolly breaks up the most ominous of partnerships as Brook can’t resist taking on the fielder at deep midwicket. Jordan Cox immediately gets off the mark with a single through cover.
 Share 1h ago 00.11 EST WICKET! Brook c Beardman b Connolly 17 (England 146-3)
 Harry Brook throws his innings away before it truly even got going. Connolly is into the attack and lures Brook into attacking a shorter ball that he scoops high into the air but picks out Beardman on the deep mid-wicket rope. A mere 23 runs in the series for the England captain.
 Share 1h ago 00.09 EST 22nd over: England 146-2 (Duckett 68, Brook 17) Johnson continues with a much better over as he contains Duckett and Brook to three singles with the field spread.
 Share 1h ago 00.08 EST Another Martin has been in touch to pose a question about whether England have erred in – again – overlooking Adil Rashid.
 “Morning Martin (well, it’s morning in London …),” he says. “Looking at the way the Aussie spinners are tying down England, will this be the game for which they really do regret not picking Rashid?”
 Moeen Ali had a similar view when he criticised the ­England set up and warned his close friend’s omission could damage their World Cup hopes next year.
 Moeen Ali warns England ‘cannot win the World Cup’ by sidelining Adil Rashid Read more Share 1h ago 00.03 EST 21st over: England 143-2 (Duckett 67, Brook 15) Renshaw finally gives up a boundary as Duckett smashes him through the covers. The off-spinner is then right back on the spot as he restricts the dangerous pair to a couple of singles.
 Share 1h ago 00.02 EST 20th over: England 137-2 (Duckett 62, Brook 14) Johnson replaces Beardman and pretty quickly releases the pressure that has been building. Duckett opens the face to ease the ball to the deep third rope and Brook soon punishes a shorter ball with a late cut to the same area of the field.
 Share 1h ago 23.55 EST 19th over: England 126-2 (Duckett 56, Brook 9) Renshaw is helping to rein in the run rate with just three singles from the over. The part-time off-spinner has one for 11 from his four overs while no other bowler has given up less than 5.5 runs an over.
 Share 1h ago 23.52 EST 18th over: England 123-2 (Duckett 54, Brook 8) Beardman ties up Brook before the England skipper pulls a single through mid-wicket. Duckett gets bat on a ball travelling well down leg to pick up one more when a wide was all but assured.
 Share 1h ago 23.48 EST 17th over: England 121-2 (Duckett 53, Brook 7) A tidy over from Renshaw has Duckett swiping away to the leg side but unable to connect with the ball. Inglis whips off the bails but Duckett has his back foot in the crease. Renshaw’s change of pace causing some concerns.
 Share 1h ago 23.45 EST 16th over: England 119-2 (Duckett 52, Brook 6) Beardman returns with a new batter at the crease. Book has no trouble dispatching a shorter ball with a crunching pull in front of square to the rope. The young quick almost has the England skipper falling over as he keeps out a yorker and slows the flow of runs.
 Share 1h ago 23.42 EST 15th over: England 113-2 (Duckett 51, Brook 1) Renshaw sends Root on his way with a clever piece of off-spin bowling as he lures the England No 3 into a loose stroke. But that only brings Harry Brook to the crease after the two teams enjoy a drinks break.
 Share 2h ago 23.36 EST WICKET! Root b Renshaw 12 (England 112-2)
 Renshaw beats Root in flight as the England No 3 looks to attack the bowler. The dip sneaks the ball under Root’s bat and takes out middle and off.
 Share 2h ago 23.35 EST 14th over: England 111-1 (Duckett 50, Root 12) Spin from both ends with Cooper Connolly coming around the wicket. Root sweeps the opening delivery fine and Travis Head misfields to give away three. Duckett drives for two more then brings up his fifty from 36 balls with a single from a pull shot.
 Share 2h ago 23.33 EST 13th over: England 105-1 (Duckett 47, Root 9) Mitch Marsh turns to spin as Renshaw takes the ball with Adam Zampa missing with back spasms. Renshaw almost makes an immediate impact as Duckett chips a defensive block up in the air and just short of the bowler. A top edge from Root off a slog sweep gives Australia some hope before the ball lands safely at deep midwicket for two. A promising over that might give a hint of what’s to come with the ball.
 Share 2h ago 23.30 EST 12th over: England 101-1 (Duckett 46, Root 6) England reach three figures from just 71 deliveries as Duckett clobbers Beardman for back-to-back boundaries. The first leaves Connolly diving desperately on the rope after a powerful pull shot from Duckett then the next is a more comfortable glance.
 Share Updated at  23.30 EST 2h ago 23.22 EST 11th over: England 89-1 (Duckett 35, Root 5) Duckett picks off a shorter, straighter ball as the left-hander crunches Edwards to the rope at fine leg. Edwards gives Root a touch too much room and he has no trouble cutting for four more.
 Share 2h ago 23.18 EST 10th over: England 79-1 (Duckett 30, Root 0) Beardman follows Bartlett in changing ends but Duckett immediately clips the young quick to the rope through midwicket. Alex Carey drops a hard pull shot struck straight at him at square leg, perhaps missing the gloves. The Test keeper gets up looking in discomfort as he walks away shaking his fingers.
 Share 2h ago 23.15 EST 9th over: England 74-1 (Duckett 25, Root 0) Jack Edwards comes into the attack as Australia take some pace off the ball. The allrounder gets the much-needed breakthrough as Banton lashes out and Marsh juggles a screamer.
 Share 2h ago 23.12 EST WICKET! Banton c Marsh b Edwards 44 (England 74-1)
 Australia needed something special to find a way back into the contest and captain Mitch Marsh steps up to pull down an absolute scream. Banton mistimes a straight drive to slice high and long to leave Marsh scampering backwards as the ball sails over his head. The skipper gets two hands to the ball and is fortunate to have it bubble in and out two times before settling into his hands. The umpires review the catch upstairs but it quickly gets cleared.
 Share 2h ago 23.07 EST 8th over: England 73-0 (Banton 44, Duckett 24) Duckett steps to the crease to face just his 10th delivery of the innings as Bartlett changes ends. The opener punches a straight drive just out of reach of the bowler’s left hand to immediately pick up a couple. Duckett gets up on his toes to punish a wider ball with a cut to the rope, then clobbers a drive past a diving Connolly and smacks the same shot again to make it three boundaries in as many balls. Another 15 runs added to England’s total as alarm bells are ringing for Australia.
 Share 2h ago 23.02 EST 7th over: England 58-0 (Banton 44, Duckett 9) Mahli Beardman is called into the attack with Australia desperate for a wicket. The 21-year-old took six of them in his ODI debut in Perth but Banton welcomes him to Hobart with a scorching boundary through a gap at mid-off. Beardman responds as he beats the bat with the ball napping back in off the seam. But Banton crunches another boundary with a drive down the ground to take another 10 from the over.
 Share 2h ago 22.59 EST 6th over: England 48-0 (Banton 34, Duckett 9) England are taking this game away from Australia as Banton clobbers Johnson for four boundaries in the over. The first might have been the best of the lot with an exquisite drive off the half-volley, then adds a second through mid-off. A shorter ball is pulled to the rope at deep square leg then Banton unloads with another, better timed, pull to the same area. An ominous 17 from the over.
 Share 2h ago 22.54 EST 5th over: England 31-0 (Banton 17, Duckett 9) Bartlett has looked the better of the two Australia quicks but Banton doesn’t need much to go wrong to find a boundary. A straighter ball is slightly overpitched and the England opener hammers a drive back past Bartlett before he can get his hands anywhere near it. Banton finds back-to-back boundaries as he whips an inswinger off his hip but is fortunate to watch a leading edge fly in the air through a vacant backward point.
 Share 2h ago 22.49 EST 4th over: England 22-0 (Banton 8, Duckett 9) Johnson yet to get the ball moving too much in the air. Duckett punishes an overpitched delivery with a sublime straight drive through Johnson’s hands and to the rope. The Australia quick has the ball drifting behind the left-handed Duckett for a wide either side of the boundary. Duckett opens up again as Johnson drops short with a pull through the gap at midwicket. Johnson will hope to have an opportunity to make amends, but that was all too loose.
 Share 2h ago 22.43 EST 3rd over: England 12-0 (Banton 8, Duckett 1) Bartlett gives Banton a bit more width and the England opener slashes in the air and barely over point. He’ll gladly accept the four runs but Bartlett won’t mind that sort of stroke.
 View image in fullscreen Khawaja on the boundary. Photograph: James Ross/AAP Share Updated at  22.57 EST 2h ago 22.41 EST 2nd over: England 8-0 (Banton 4, Duckett 1) Spencer Johnson takes the new ball and Banton glances for a couple that are called leg byes. Banton chips a fuller ball off his toes for two behind square. Australia rise as one with a shout for lbw as Johnson, coming around the wicket, gets the ball to nip back into Banton. Just a few issues with that one as the ball pitched outside leg stump, struck the pad outside the line and kept drifting further away. Don’t ask, don’t get.
 Share 3h ago 22.35 EST 1st over: England 3-0 (Banton 2, Duckett 1) Bartlett immediately has the ball shaping away from the right-hander Banton. The opener is coming off a match-defining knock of 121 from 99 balls in Adelaide, and starts with a pair of singles today in Hobart. Duckett picks up a single with a glance to fine leg.
 Share 3h ago 22.30 EST Xavier Bartlett has the white pill in his hand and is at the top of his mark as the sun belts down at Bellerive Oval. Tom Banton marks centre with Ben Duckett at the non-striker’s end. Let’s play …
 Share 3h ago 22.28 EST We’re about five minutes away from what some of us are here for – the third ODI between Australia and England. Begin to shift your minds away from the ongoing sandpaper saga by learning more about how, ahem, cheaters still might prosper, as the Secret Cricket Coach tells us a tale … 
 double quotation mark I once played in a one-day semi-final. We were in a very tight spot when I edged the ball to the keeper. I didn’t walk. The opposition couldn’t believe it. They crowded around me, furious, and I was getting plenty of abuse.
 I managed to get a single and when I reached the other end the umpire said: ‘You didn’t nick that did you? You are a walker.’ ‘Yep, that’s right,’ I replied.
 I built a reputation as a ‘walker’ so I could cheat when it mattered most – and it worked | The Secret Cricket Coach Read more Share 3h ago 22.23 EST David Warner is seated next to Khawaja and ready to have his say as he starts by making the point that he does not want to see further sanctions imposed … 
 double quotation mark Look, we put our hands up. We accept what Cricket Australia handed down to us. It’s not about penalties. It’s just about coming out with transparency and accountability in which, Todd’s acknowledged on CA’s behalf about the culture at the time with the players and CA .So I respect that again. And I think everyone just wants to see cricket played on our TV.
 Yes, people want to talk about moving on. But in this safe environment, we want every single person that’s there to be able to speak. We all want to move on. There’s no clearer thing from everyone than we want to move on. The question is, will this allow us to move on? That’s the question that has to be asked.
